mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary conditions, which can lead to decreased corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when FEDFUNDS is high, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative despite HOUST increase, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative with low UNRATE, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) is low and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is high, it indicates economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative with strong labor metrics, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong supply chains, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative despite INDPRO growth, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising real consumption (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days when RSAFS crosses a threshold.
failure_condition: Returns are negative with RSAFS growth, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, high FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE signal late-cycle dynamics, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive in late-cycle, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in FEDFUNDS below 4% indicates easing, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when FEDFUNDS drops below 4%, or Rank IC < 0.03.
